articles.title: Exclusive-US chip curbs, distillation crackdown threaten Chinese AI model development, sources say
articles.summary: Nov 26 (Reuters) - China's Z.AI has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship AI model, while rival Moonshot AI expects the interval between major releases...
articles.body:
Nov 26 (Reuters) - China's Z.AI has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship AI model, while rival Moonshot AI expects the interval between major releases could double from six months to a year or longer if it loses access to overseas computing power, people familiar with the matter said.

The previously unreported details show how efforts by ‌US AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic to prevent distillation, a technique in which developers train models using answers generated by more capable ones, have slowed Chinese AI development. Washington's latest ‌chip restrictions threaten further delays.

The measures jeopardise a key advantage that has helped Chinese AI companies challenge their American rivals despite years of export controls: the ability to develop competitive models at substantially lower cost.

A US Commerce Department rule that took ​effect on November 19 imposes licensing requirements aimed at restricting Chinese companies' access to large amounts of computing power from advanced US chips in overseas data centres, targeting a means of accessing Nvidia processors without importing them.

Z.AI, also known as Zhipu AI, had planned to release its next flagship model, GLM-5.5, this month but has yet to do so, two people familiar with the matter said on condition of anonymity.

The model, designed with roughly 3 trillion parameters - a measure of its size - has been held up partly by increasingly effective safeguards against distillation, one of the people said.

Z.AI had hoped to complete training and release the model by ‌year-end, but the new US computing restrictions could push its launch into ⁠the first quarter of 2027 or later, the person said.

Z.AI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

On Monday, the company released GLM-5.4, built on an existing model with 750 billion parameters. Z.AI says a new design enables it to match the performance of models with 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameters.

Anthropic ( ANT ) ⁠said in September it had observed nearly 200 million exchanges with its Claude models linked to suspected distillation campaigns, attributing them to Chinese developers including Alibaba ( BABA ), Moonshot and Z.AI.

OpenAI has made similar accusations against individuals associated with Moonshot. Anthropic has described measures it uses to detect and block unauthorised distillation, while OpenAI has also reported efforts to disrupt such activity.

Moonshot did not respond immediately to a request for comment. It has previously rejected suggestions ​that ​its Kimi K3 model's performance was achieved via distillation, telling China's National Business Daily in July that its performance ​gains came from original changes to underlying architecture.

articles.title: Another Nvidia romance draws scrutiny: Jay Puri's ties to executive at a firm linked to China
articles.summary: Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia executive who led its global sales team, is facing scrutiny over his relationship with Cenly Chen, a former senior executive
articles.body: Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia executive who led its global sales team, is facing scrutiny over his relationship with Cenly Chen, a former senior executive at US-based server maker Super Micro Computer. The couple dated for several years and married on March 7 this year, according to records. Their relationship has come under the spotlight amid a US investigation into allegations that Super Micro servers loaded with Nvidia chips were diverted to China.Chen was Super Micro's chief growth officer and regularly dealt with Puri when the company was seeking access to Nvidia's chips for its customers, according to current and former employees of both companies, The Wall Street Journal reported.She also accompanied Super Micro CEO Charles Liang on visits to Nvidia's offices, where he pressed the chipmaker to supply products to the company's customers.How their professional roles overlappedDuring Super Micro sales meetings, Chen encouraged employees to approach her with questions related to Nvidia, positioning herself as the company's key contact on such matters, employees said.Puri, meanwhile, headed Nvidia's global sales team, which was responsible for deciding how the company's latest chips were allocated among customers. He joined Nvidia in 2005 after spending two decades at Sun Microsystems and working at other technology companies. He stepped back from his global sales role in July but remained a senior adviser.Chen denied that her relationship with Puri influenced her professional decisions. “I never had to rely on personal relationships for professional gain,” she said in an email as quoted in the WSJ report.She also said she was not involved in selecting or procuring chips for Super Micro. “I dealt with Super Micro’s customers and the customer decided the chips they bought,” Chen said, adding, “I was not involved in the selection or procurement of the chips.”Super Micro said Chen “did not manage Supermicro’s overall relationship with Nvidia or our procurement of Nvidia GPUs. Our relationship with Nvidia spans dozens of teams, functions and projects.” The company added that allocation of Nvidia chips to its customers was determined through a multi-department process.Super Micro's China-linked chip probeThe scrutiny comes as Super Micro faces a US investigation into an alleged scheme to divert servers containing high-end Nvidia chips to China.On March 19, the US justice department unsealed charges against Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, a sales manager and a third-party broker. The indictment accused the three of conspiring to smuggle more than $500 million worth of servers containing Nvidia chips into China.Prosecutors alleged that the accused directed an unidentified company in Southeast Asia to place orders worth around $2.5 billion for Super Micro servers in 2024 and 2025, before diverting at least $510 million worth of equipment to China.Super Micro was not named as a defendant and has said it was a victim of the alleged scheme. Chen was not named in the indictment and said she had not been contacted by federal law enforcement. The company said it was cooperating with authorities and had cut ties with the individuals charged.Liaw has pleaded not guilty and resigned from Super Micro's board in March. The third-party broker has pleaded guilty under an agreement with prosecutors.How the relationship came under scrutinyChen's relationship with Puri came under renewed attention after a shareholder lawsuit alleged that she played a role in Super Micro's acquisition of Nvidia chips. Short seller Muddy Waters also highlighted the couple's ties in a research report earlier this month.Chen spent nearly two decades at Super Micro after joining the San Jose-based company in 2008. She later became its chief growth officer, overseeing the sales team dealing with some of its biggest customers. She left the company after Nvidia's annual conference in March and was named CEO of cloud services company ChronoScale, which was spun out of Applied Digital, another Nvidia partner.Wes Cummins, CEO of Applied Digital and chairman of ChronoScale, said Chen had helped Applied Digital establish its cloud business and had advocated with Nvidia on behalf of customers. He acknowledged that her relationship with Puri created the appearance of a conflict of interest, but said he was unaware of Super Micro receiving any special treatment from Nvidia.Cummins also said the relationship had prevented ChronoScale and Applied Digital from accessing some Nvidia assistance available to customers because of the disclosed conflict of interest.Puri and Chen's relationship was known to people who worked with them. They were photographed together at the San Francisco Opera's annual masked gala in September 2024 and later attended a California Academy of Sciences gala in April with other Nvidia executives and their spouses.The developments come amid scrutiny of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's personal and professional relationships with executives at companies linked to allegations of chip diversion to China.Huang had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed International, another Nvidia customer. Some US officials suspect Alice Huang of having worked with Chinese intelligence.Both Megaspeed and Super Micro are dealing with justice department investigations into allegations of chip smuggling to China.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Global markets rebound as tech shares recover and tariff fears ease
articles.summary: Shares advanced in Europe and Asia on Thursday, while US markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.View on euronews
articles.body:
Buying of stocks tied to artificial intelligence helped push benchmarks in Asia higher, though investors have been growing cautious over the AI trade. They are also watching for the impact of the latest tariff hikes Washington plans to impose on China, the European Union and other trading partners.

In early European trading, Germany's DAX jumped 1.8% to 25,131.36, while the CAC 40 in Paris climbed 1.6% to 8,110.88. Britain's FTSE 100 added 1.3% to 10,563.62.

The future for the S&P 500 was up 0.3%. The future for the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged 0.2% higher. US markets will reopen for a shortened trading session on Friday.

Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 0.9% to 57,499.16. OpenAI investor SoftBank Group jumped 7.3%, while memory maker Kioxia Holdings surged 12.6%. Shares of chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron were up 0.6%.

South Korea's benchmark Kospi index added 0.3% to 4,711.21 after a 6.2% drop a day earlier. Samsung Electronics gained 0.4%, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix rose 2.2%.

Taiwan's Taiex was 2.5% higher. But shares of its leading chipmaker TSMC, or Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., edged 0.2% lower.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was 1.2% higher at 22,226.88. The Shanghai Composite index was up less than 0.1% at 3,476.88.

Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.8% to 8,763.80.

Wall Street closed mixed ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The benchmark S&P 500 index lost 0.3% on Wednesday after falling as much as 3.2% earlier in the day. The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite closed 0.6% lower, after recovering from a drop of as much as 4.6%. The Dow industrials gained 0.3%.

Nvidia fell 3.9% as AI shares lost steam for a second day after Jensen Huang's comeback as CEO. On Wednesday, S&P Global Ratings warned it could downgrade Nvidia's credit rating over concerns surrounding its management and governance.

Broadcom, which had fallen sharply earlier in the day, was 0.1% lower at the close. Anthropic, which began public trading last week, recovered from an early drop and ended 1.1% higher, though still below its IPO, or initial public offering, price of $83 (€72.10) per share.

In commodities trading, oil prices climbed early Thursday as tensions in the Middle East persisted even as global oil supply continued to recover.

Brent crude, the international standard, was 0.2% higher at $90.79 (€78.86) per barrel. It was trading at approximately $72 (€62.57) a barrel before the war began in late February. Benchmark US crude gained 0.4% to $84.10 (€73.06) per barrel.

The US dollar slipped to 159.14 Japanese yen from 159.16 yen. The euro was trading at $1.0975, up from $1.0974.

articles.title: IT sector employees seek national AI layoff policy as automation threatens jobs; unions and experts want NASSCOM and government to set minimum severance, advance notice, redeployment and reskilling rules for employees who lose work
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing job uncertainty with regards to adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), especially in the IT sector, workers are now seeking protection.
articles.body: Amid the ongoing job uncertainty with regards to adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), especially in the IT sector, workers are now seeking protection. India’s information technology industry needs a common policy for reporting job losses caused by artificial intelligence and protecting workers affected by automation.Employee representatives and workforce experts are seeking minimum standards for advance notice, severance pay, internal redeployment and reskilling, rather than leaving these decisions entirely to individual employers.Policy for AI layoffsNascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has approached government authorities over concerns about mass layoffs, forced resignations and unfair employment practices.It is now seeking a separate policy framework specifically addressing job losses linked to AI.The proposed framework would require companies to record and disclose the number of positions eliminated because of AI, employees shifted to different roles within the organisation and workers retrained for new jobs, according to an ET report.It would also establish minimum expectations for employers to explore internal transfers before making employees redundant, offer fair compensation and help those affected find alternative employment.Harpreet Singh Saluja, president of NITES said companies should be able to adopt new technologies but must also account for the impact on employees’ livelihoods. He said technological progress should not come at the cost of leaving workers without adequate support.Saluja told the financial daily that employees and the government should have access to clear information on the number of workers affected, the reasons for eliminating positions and the extent to which technology is directly replacing jobs.He said employers should make genuine efforts to retrain employees or move them into other positions within the organisation before eliminating roles because of AI or automation. Saluja also called for adequate advance notice, fair severance packages and the settlement of outstanding dues. Reskilling, he stressed, should provide employees with meaningful opportunities to take up new work, rather than being limited to a handful of online courses.Need for reliable dataTeamLease Digital estimates that over the next 18-24 months, 30% of jobs in the technology sector could face compression, while AI could significantly augment another 45% of roles. The remaining 25% could move towards higher-value work involving AI, data, cloud computing and cybersecurity.Employees are looking for exit packages similar to those provided by Microsoft and Canva. Under Microsoft's voluntary exit programme in India, eligible employees received one month's base salary for every completed year of service, along with health insurance and career transition assistance.Neeti Sharma, chief executive of staffing firm TeamLease Digital, told ET that the IT industry currently has no clearly defined, common policy setting minimum requirements for severance, redeployment or reskilling when employees lose their jobs because of AI.She called for baseline safeguards covering advance communication, fair exit compensation, opportunities to move into other roles within the company and employer-funded reskilling. Sharma also said companies should maintain data on positions eliminated due to AI, employees transferred internally and workers trained for different roles.Ravi Venkatesan, founder of the Institute for Human Flourishing (IHF), said the matter required a national-level response instead of separate approaches by individual companies. He suggested that an industry association such as NASSCOM should consult its members and prioritise disclosure of workforce reductions.Venkatesan said society needed reliable data and evidence on these developments to determine the appropriate policy response. He also called for a national safety net that defines employers’ responsibilities towards workers who lose their jobs and clarifies the government's role in helping them transition to new employment.He argued that fair severance should be governed by a national policy rather than left solely to individual company rules. He also stressed the need to establish what responsibilities employers and the government should share in helping displaced workers acquire the skills required for new jobs.Canva, which announced a restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, equivalent to 22% of its workforce, offered those leaving the company at least six months' salary, healthcare coverage where applicable and career support. The company maintained that the positions being eliminated were not being replaced by AI.ET had earlier reported that employees affected by Qualcomm's workforce reduction in India were offered two months' notice pay, an additional month's salary for every year of service, continued insurance coverage for a year, stock awards and placement assistance, among other benefits. These details were provided by employees familiar with the exit arrangements and were not publicly confirmed by the company.However, despite growing demands for common industry-wide safeguards, there is little indication that companies are jointly developing such a framework.Pareekh Jain, chief executive of EIIRTrend, said companies had not begun discussions on a common policy, even as employees were raising the issue. He said workers wanted fair exit packages comparable to those offered by Microsoft and Canva. Some were also approaching the government for tax relief on their final settlements.The absence of transparent data is another obstacle to determining the actual extent of AI-driven job losses, said Kamal Karanth, co-founder of Xpheno. He observed that the last period when the industry had some visibility into workforce reductions was during the pandemic-related layoffs between late 2020 and 2022.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Walmart won't resort to 'gimmicks' to get Black Friday shoppers in early
articles.summary: Walmart US chief merchant told Business Insider the retailer is looking to win Black Friday shoppers with great items and deals, not door prizes.
articles.body:
Door prizes have become a popular way for stores to boost Black Friday traffic — but not at Walmart.

The company's US chief merchant told BI she intends to win shoppers by offering the best deals.

"We're not going to pay people to get in line," she said.

Walmart is taking an old-school approach to retail's busiest weekend of the year .

Although several retailers are rolling out door prizes like swag bags and gift cards to boost Black Friday visits, Walmart's US chief merchant Julie Barber told Business Insider she's letting the deals do the talking.

"We're not going to do gimmicks. We're not going to pay people to get in line. We're going to have amazing items in the store, and that's going to drive people in," she said.

That's a sharp contrast with rival Target, which will give away gift cards worth at least $25 to the first hundred shoppers at each of its stores on Black Friday. One winner at each location will get a $1,000 card.

Kohl's is likewise offering $5 to $100 gift cards to the first 200 shoppers at its stores, and Lowe's is again giving its Black Friday Buckets to the first 50 rewards members who show up at participating locations. In addition to free Lowe's merchandise, some winners will receive appliances worth up to $2,000.

Barber spent this week jetting around the country to check on how Walmart stores — and their competitors — are prepping for the holiday rush.

This year, she says Walmart customers are laser-focused on value , with seven in ten survey respondents telling the company that lower prices would make their holiday shopping easier. That translates to the company emphasizing new products and low prices.

She said that Thanksgiving week is typically the largest-selling period of the year for TVs, but Walmart is extending Black Friday deals beyond traditional gifts and electronics to offer discounts on more everyday essentials. For example, Walmart will be running a big sale on vehicle tires.

Last week, CFO John David Rainey said the online sales growth of more than 20% year over year is more than offsetting a slight decline of in-person shopping.

"Between in-store shopping and digital fulfillment, we have more volume going through our US stores than ever before," he said during Walmart's third quarter earnings call.

Barber said that her store teams are heading into the holiday rush with the highest inventory levels that they've had all year.

"We're set up pretty well, I think, for both the in-store and online shopper," she said.

And even though the holiday season is starting earlier and includes more individual sale events on the calendar leading up to Christmas, Barber said her team makes sure there's enough compelling deals to make the annual Black Friday spree worthwhile.

"We plan it out where there's something new and special that happens every time we have an event," she said.

articles.title: The small-cap Santa Claus rally is on — but a December Fed rate hike has spoiled it before: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: A December Fed hike could take a big bite out of small caps' favorite holiday trade.
articles.body:
Small-cap stocks sat down to their favorite holiday trade on Tuesday. History says a Fed hike can leave them with a much smaller helping than usual.

The trade is Jeff Hirsch's "Small Cap Feast." Buy the Russell 2000 at the close on the Tuesday before Thanksgiving, then sell on the second trading day of the new year — Jan. 5 this time.

It rides through the Santa Claus rally , which his father, Yale Hirsch, discovered. It has worked in 36 of the past 47 years, according to the Stock Trader's Almanac, which Hirsch publishes and edits.

This year, the Fed meets Dec. 9, right in the middle of it. After Wednesday's hotter-than-expected inflation report , Polymarket bettors put the chances of a rate hike at about 96%.

That has been the trade's weak spot. In the nine years since 1983 when the Fed hiked during the trade, the Russell 2000's ( ^RUT ) median gain was about 1%, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. Without a hike, it was about 4%.

Three of the four worst runs since 1983 came in hike years, including 2018, when the Fed raised rates days before stocks' Christmas Eve rout. The fourth, 2024, came after the Fed cut rates but warned that fewer cuts were coming.

Nine years is a small sample, and four came back-to-back from 2015 to 2018. Leave those out, and the median in hike years is still about 1%.

The trade's recent record is thinner too. It has worked only half the time over the past dozen years.

Drew Pettit, chief investment strategist at Roundhill Investments, is watching credit spreads — the extra yield investors demand to lend to companies instead of the US government.

"The signal that the market is telling the Fed they're making a mistake to me is the correlation between spreads and rates," Pettit said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang on Tuesday. Small caps lagged in the latest pullback as spreads widened and rates rose, he added.

On the same show, Sherwood News' Luke Kawa said what the Fed has seen lately points to "more hikes, full steam ahead."

Small caps did come into the trade in better shape than Big Tech, falling far less than the Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ) over the past month. And six of the nine hike years still ended higher. A thinner feast is still arguably a feast.

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, sounded less festive on Market Hang on Monday. His firm's data, he said, suggest "the Fed is still taking away the punch bowl."

articles.title: Black Friday is about to deliver a reality check to the retail bears
articles.summary: The US consumer is looking surprisingly strong at the start of the holiday shopping season.
articles.body:
The holiday season officially kicks off today, giving investors a break from all things Nvidia ( NVDA ) and reinstated CEO Jensen Huang.

Thanksgiving Day deal shopping after consuming your turkey begins this afternoon. Black Friday is coming tomorrow.

And despite all the noise about inflation, interest rates, and consumer anxiety, there are reasons to believe retailers could have a very strong holiday season, and their stock prices could perform well into year-end.

1. Retailers are already showing signs of life

Target just delivered a strong third quarter. Sales climbed 7.1%. Comparable sales increased 5.6%. And store traffic was up 5%.

More people are walking into Target despite gas over $4 a gallon. They're buying more merchandise. And digital sales are growing, too.

"At the start of the year we were laser focused on what our strategy needed to be, and it's getting back to the unique lane that we play in retail, and that's always going to be a combination of leading with style and design, and of course, incredible value," Target CEO Michael Fiddelke told Yahoo Finance . "The 'I can't believe the quality of this,' or 'I can't believe I found it at Target at a price point' that makes the smile get wider. Once someone turns over the price tag, that's when we're at our best, and then you add to that, continuing to make the experience even better and more consistent. Like that's been the work we're doing, and in the categories where we've leaned in most to drive change, we really like the response we're seeing."

That's not a consumer who has completely shut down.

Target also raised its full-year sales growth outlook to around 6%.

The stock is hovering around a 52-week high, up 79% on the year.

And it's not just about Target. We're seeing retailers such as Walmart ( WMT ) fight aggressively for consumer dollars with better assortments, compelling prices, and more reasons to shop. They are winning, as underscored by Walmart CFO John David Rainey, who said on Sozzi Unleashed that the holidays have started well.

Best Buy ( BBY ) is also in the winning column — it just reported its best sales growth in years this week.

The key takeaway: Retailers are entering the holiday season with some real momentum.

2. The US consumer still has money to spend

The consumer remains a major engine of the US economy. Household finances have held up despite major inflationary pressure, income growth is providing support, and rising stock and home values have helped many households feel wealthier.

articles.title: Man booked Rs 86 lakh flat, paid Rs 14.76 lakh and Rs 25.05 lakh in EMIs as construction stalled; District Commission ordered refund with 9% interest, EMI reimbursement, loan settlement, but State Commission rejects plea for more relief
articles.summary: You book a flat and pay a booking amount while also getting a home loan to finance the remaining payment.
articles.body: You book a flat and pay a booking amount while also getting a home loan to finance the remaining payment. However after a few years you discover that the project has allegedly been abandoned by the developer. What do you do?In one such case, the District Consumer Commission ordered the real estate developer to refund the homebuyer’s booking amount, reimburse earlier EMIs and settle the loan liability.What the case is aboutA homebuyer booked a 237-square-yard residential floor in a real estate project in Sonipat in February 2017. He paid Rs 14.76 lakh towards the property and also got a home loan.According to his complaint, the possession was promised by October 2019. However, the homebuyer alleged that when he visited the construction site in December 2019, work had stopped and he learnt that the project had been abandoned.He also alleged that the finance company had disbursed Rs 67,47,091 directly to the developer without verifying the construction stage.The homebuyer said he had paid Rs 25,05,615 in EMIs and sent a legal notice in January 2020 seeking cancellation of the allotment. He relied on the tripartite agreement, arguing that the developer was responsible for repaying the loan to the finance company and returning his contribution, subject to applicable administrative charges.The real estate developer contested the complaint. It claimed that possession for fit-out purposes had been offered through a letter in August 2018, and that the homebuyer had outstanding dues. It also challenged the complaint on limitation, jurisdiction and consumer-status grounds, alleging that the property had been booked for commercial purposes. The finance company maintained that the homebuyer obligation to repay the loan continued independently of the dispute with the developer.The District Commission rejected the developer's force majeure defence, noting that it had not produced evidence to establish that the delay resulted from circumstances beyond its control.It observed: "admittedly, there is inordinate delay in handing over the possession of the flat in question which amounts to deficiency in service."The commission also found that the developer had not established that the homebuyer was dealing in real estate for commercial purposes. It held both respondents guilty of deficiency in service.The District Commission directed the real estate to refund Rs 14.76 lakh with interest at 9% per annum from the respective dates of deposit. If the refund was not made within four weeks of receipt of the order, the interest rate would rise to 12% per annum until realisation. It also awarded Rs 1 lakh for mental agony and harassment and Rs 25,000 towards litigation costs.Separately, the developer was directed to pay the loan amount to the finance company, reimburse the EMIs paid from May 2017 to September 2020 with interest at 9% from the date of each payment, and settle the future EMI and loan liability with the lender.Why District Consumer Commission ruled in favour of homebuyer and State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission dismissed later pleaHowever, the homebuyer appealed because he wanted reimbursement extended to the installments paid during the complaint proceedings. He sought reimbursement of EMIs paid up to May 2024, which he quantified at Rs 60,56,700. He also asked for litigation costs to be increased from Rs 25,000 to Rs 5 lakh.The State Commission noted that the finance company had not appealed against the District Commission's order, which had therefore attained finality in relation to that respondent.It also rejected the lender's limitation objection because the homebuyer’s application seeking condonation of delay in filing the appeal had already been allowed. Since the homebuyer’s principal grievance concerned the developer, the commission said it would not discuss the finance company's other submissions in the appeal.The central question was whether the District Commission's order needed modification. The State Commission examined the existing directions on reimbursement and the future loan liability.It explained: "A perusal of the above referred clause (ii) makes it clear that District Commission has not only directed OP1 to pay the EMI amount to OP 2 from May 2017 to Sept 2020, but also directed OP1 to settle the future EMI/loan amount with OP2."The commission considered this direction sufficient to address the homebuyer’s grievance.It stated: "Since Ld. District Commission has already directed respondent1 to settle the future EMI/Loan amount with respondent no 2, we are of the considered view that the grievance of appellant has already been taken care of by Ld. District Commission."It therefore rejected the argument that the District Commission had failed to provide for the loan liability during the complaint proceedings. It also found no grounds to increase litigation costs to Rs 5 lakh.Concluding that the original order required no modification, the State Commission observed: "Thus, in view of above discussion we find no infirmity and illegality in the impugned order passed by the Ld. District Forum which needs modification by this Commission."The appeal was dismissed, with both sides directed to bear their own costs. The original relief remained in place, but the homebuyer did not obtain the additional modification he sought.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Wall Street is in chaos. Don't let it ruin your Thanksgiving.
articles.summary: A few Thanksgiving Day investing reminders.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving has arrived. And with it, the official start of the holiday season.

I know a lot of you are going to sit down with your families today, carve up the inflationary turkey, have a few stiff drinks, and probably check your portfolios somewhere between the mashed potatoes and protein-packed dessert.

And I will say this: What a week to be an investor — whether casual or hardcore active trader.

We've had a massive market sell-off. We've watched Nvidia's ( NVDA ) super-important stock swing wildly in price. We've seen Jensen Huang return to the CEO chair and remind everybody just how much influence one person can have over this market, if not the entire world.

I want to serve up a few things to consider.

First, don't confuse a bad week in the market with a bad investment strategy. Markets go up. Markets go down. Your job isn't to react to every headline. It's to know what you own and why you own it.

Use this time to reconnect with what you own and why. If those theses have been blown up, acknowledge it and take action.

Second, don't fall in love with a stock. Not Nvidia, with its no-succession-plan-loving leader back at the helm. Not any company. Great businesses can be terrible investments at the wrong price. And no CEO, no matter how brilliant, is bigger than the fundamentals.

Thank you, HPE CEO Antonio Neri, for reminding me of that this week .

Third, remember that volatility is part of the deal in investing. If you want the long-term rewards of investing, you have to be willing to live through the uncomfortable days like we are seeing right now. Sometimes the hardest thing to do is absolutely nothing.

And finally, don't forget what all this investing is supposed to be for.

It's supposed to help you build a better life. More freedom. More opportunity. More time with the people who actually matter in your life (and that's not Jensen Huang).

Not another reason to stare at your iPhone Duo while your family is sitting across the table.

To everyone who watches Yahoo Finance, reads our stories, challenges us, agrees with us, disagrees with us — thank you. Seriously. We don't take your time or your trust for granted.

I'm grateful you're riding with me. I'm grateful we get to do this every day. And I'm grateful to be part of your financial journey.

Enjoy the turkey. Hug your family. Dress up your pet in a cute holiday costume. Call somebody you haven't spoken to in a while. If you have investing questions, get at me on X @BrianSozzi — I will obviously be online waiting for the next Jensen headline.

The market will be here on Friday, as will I.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: Higher borrowing costs weigh on G4 economies, cloud 2027 rate hike outlook: Report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Higher borrowing costs are beginning to weigh more heavily on business demand across major developed economies, potentially reducing the need
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Higher borrowing costs are beginning to weigh more heavily on business demand across major developed economies, potentially reducing the need for further interest rate increases in 2027, even as central banks are widely expected to raise rates by 25 basis points each in December, according to a report by S&P Global.Business activity growth across the US, UK, Japan and the eurozone slowed for a second consecutive month in November, hitting its weakest level since June, as elevated prices, economic uncertainty and higher borrowing costs continued to constrain demand.The latest purchasing managers' index (PMI) data showed that businesses were increasingly reporting weaker sales due to rising borrowing costs, ahead of the anticipated rate hikes next month."If sustained, the demand slowdown could potentially limit the need for further increases into 2027," S&P Global said, as quoted by ANI.The report noted that while all four major central banks are expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in December, the outlook for further tightening next year remains uncertain."There is less certainty over the extent to which rates will need to rise further in 2027, with all the major central banks data dependent," it said.Lower global crude oil prices provided some relief on the inflation front in November, easing price pressures across all four economies. However, selling price inflation remained among the highest levels recorded over the past three years, indicating that cost pressures had not fully subsided.Higher costs also affected labour market conditions, with employment growth slowing in the US, while the UK and eurozone reported job losses. S&P Global said policymakers would closely track business output, new orders and employment trends to assess companies' pricing power and workers' ability to negotiate higher wages."November’s PMI data already saw increased reporting by companies of the demand dampening impact of higher borrowing costs," the report said.Central banks across major economies have been pursuing monetary tightening to contain inflation. The European Central Bank has raised rates twice by 25 basis points each this year, while the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England have each delivered a 25-basis-point hike. The Bank of Japan has also continued its longer-term monetary tightening cycle.In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has also been adjusting its monetary policy in response to inflation and growth conditions, with its rate decisions closely watched for their impact on borrowing costs, credit demand and economic activity.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Yasir Al-Rumayyan explaining why Saudi Arabia PIF bought Newcastle United
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia PIF Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan flew in for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal. He didn’t pick a bad one.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia PIF Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan flew in for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal.

As always though, when Yasir Al-Rumayyan is part of a PIF visiting group to Tyneside, it also sparks intrigue as to other potential reasons for his/their visit.

On Wednesday, an exclusive from The Athletic reported that the Newcastle United owners were now planning to sell a stake in the club that would enable a new party (or parties) to own 25% of NUFC.

The report stating that this would be done by issuing new shares.

So if a 25% share in the club was sold via the issue of new shares, the Saudi Arabia PIF and the Reuben family (Chris Waugh at The Athletic has on Thursday confirmed that they as well as PIF would see their shareholding diluted) would see their ownership of the club reduce respectively from 84% to 63% and 16% to 12%.

The Athletic reporting on Wednesday that the idea with selling the 25% stake in NUFC is not for any money to go directly to PIF or the Reubens, instead it is intended that the money generated by selling a quarter ownership of the club would be put towards spending on the infrastructure, the state of the art training ground and a new stadium. With estimates of a club current valuation now of up to £2billion, that would potentially mean up to £500million raised towards financing the new Newcastle United stadium and training ground.

Unsurprisingly this sparked a lot of conjecture in the media and amongst fans.

Was the Yasir Al-Rumayyan visit to Tyneside not simply to watch the Arsenal match and indeed, what did The Athletic exclusive potentially suggest about future plans of the Saudi Arabia PIF majority ownership?

I think what is key is to go back and revisit exactly why PIF bought a controlling stake in Newcastle United.

This below is Yasir Al-Rumayyan handily explaining himself why the Saudi Arabia PIF bought the majority ownership of the club.

Yasir Al-Rumayyan speaking on 4 October 2022, a few days before the first anniversary of the Newcastle United takeover:

"We bought the whole team (Newcastle United) for £350m, instead of only having 30 per cent in another team (Manchester United) for £700m.

"You can see Chelsea was sold for $3.5bn (£2.5bn).

"So, my potential now is to go from £350m to at least $3.5bn (£2.5bn).

"Football of course is one of the most important sports there is, whether domestically (in Saudi Arabia) or abroad.

"It is the number one sport in the world and why the English Premier League?

"Well, because it is the best league in the world, no other league competes with it.

"There are 20 teams, three are relegated, three are promoted, the advantage of the Premier League is that any of the 20 teams can beat the best team in the league.

"When we looked at it, we looked at it from a financial perspective.

"By the way, it wasn't the first offer we got regarding a football team. We looked in Italy, France and the UK as well.

"In the UK there was a team (Manchester United) that approached us on the basis that we take 30 per cent of the ownership and (on the condition that) we don't interfere at all in terms of managing the club, for £700m.

"Then we bought Newcastle, who offered us 100 per cent of the ownership, but Amanda Staveley and her husband who got us the opportunity told us, 'We like it so much, we would like to be with you'….and that was perfect.

"Then came the Reuben family, who are one of the biggest property investors (in the UK), saying that, 'We would like to come with you', and these are one of the biggest investors in (the City of) Newcastle (Upon Tyne).

"I said, 'Perfect! Tell them to come'. So now they (Amanda Staveley, her husband and the Reubens) have a skin in the game."

Just under five months later, Amanda Staveley was speaking at the FT Business of Football Summit in Mayfair, London on Thursday 2 March 2023 and she then gave further insight into why the Saudi Arabia PIF had decided to buy Newcastle United:

"When we walked into a Newcastle United game we said why spend X Billion when you can spend three hundred and some million and put in….I think we have put in two hundred plus to date of new money since we bought the club.

"We had a particular business plan, based on a five, ten, fifteen year timeline.

"Critical to that plan was making sure we had the right partners.

"So making sure (Saudi Arabia) PIF, who are very long-term investors.

"Hoping potentially there might be the chance of Champions League.

"I love the valuations that are reflecting in Chelsea….because it makes our valuation look very compelling.

"We bought the club at under two times revenue.

"When you are looking at five to seven times revenue, that is a lot of money."

What was said by Yasir Al-Rumayyan just over four years ago (and then Amanda Staveley just over three and a half years ago) very much fits in with what is happening now, in my opinion. Their prediction/expectation of huge growth in the value of Newcastle United has become reality and now further steps to be taken in order to help push that valuation far far higher. Part of that plan appears to now be to bring in money from other investors which will help to finance essential infrastructure projects, namely the stadium and training ground. Injecting cash from elsewhere via an issue of new shares that then reduces the levels of money that may then needed to be loaned to help cover the spending, plus it also reduces the exposure of the Saudi Arabia PIF and the Reubens.

articles.title: Lazio Bracing Themselves for Inevitable January Transfer Ban
articles.summary: While the official confirmation won’t arrive until December, Lazio reportedly realise they won’t be allowed to operate in the market in January.Lazio Have Be...
articles.body:
While the official confirmation won't arrive until December, Lazio reportedly realise they won't be allowed to operate in the market in January.

Lazio Have Been Struggling to Keep Their Market Open

Against all odds, the Aquile currently lead the Serie A standings. However, their balance sheet paints a less bright picture of the club's general status. In the summer of 2025, Lazio were infamously banned from any transfer activities after failing to meet the required financial standards.

Claudio Lotito and Angelo Fabiani (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

Last January, the club sold Taty Castellanos and Matteo Guendouzi, earning enough capital gains to prevent another summer ban. However, the Biancocelesti still failed to meet the required Squad Cost Ratio threshold of 0.7, so they were forced to operate under net-zero restrictions in the summer of 2026, meaning they could only sign new players using freshly generated transfer funds.

Rating Lazio 2026 Summer Transfer Campaign: The Zero-Cost Masterclass

Luckily for Lazio, Sporting Director Angelo Fabiani was able to deliver despite the restrictions, recruiting the likes of Davide Frattesi, Josip Sutalo, and Albert Gudmundsson. The club also sold Mario Gila, Alessio Romagnoli, and Ivan Provedel, but it wasn't necessarily sufficient to balance the books.

According to Il Messaggero (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ), Fabiani and Lazio president Claudio Lotito are both aware that a transfer ban in January is considered almost inevitable. By the end of November, the club must present its financial statements to the supervisory committee, which then hands down its verdict in December.

Claudio Lotito (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

While it was recently suggested that Lotito could try to plug the deficit by deferring taxes or collecting sponsorship money in advance, the hierarchy believes these figures won't be sufficient to settle the situation. Therefore, the hierarchy has seemingly accepted the outcome.

Why Lazio Aren't Keen on Net-Zero Market

The Roman newspaper adds that the best Lazio could hope for at the moment is another net-zero market, but Lotito and Fabiani aren't too enticed by this possibility. After all, they would only be able to sign new players by offloading some of their own, whereas they had already promised Gennaro Gattuso they wouldn't cash in on any important players in the middle of the season.

articles.title: What is EPFO Amnesty Scheme 2026? Importance of one-time window to regularise legacy PF trusts
articles.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) introduced the Amnesty Scheme, 2026 as a significant regulatory initiative aimed at addressing a
articles.body: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) introduced the Amnesty Scheme, 2026 as a significant regulatory initiative aimed at addressing a long-standing compliance gap involving establishments that operate their own Provident Fund (PF) trust without having obtained the requisite formal exemption under the PF statute.Over the years, several establishments formed independent PF trust to administer benefits for their employees. In many instances, these trusts obtained recognition under the Income-tax Act, 1961 and operated as employer-managed. However, recognition under Income tax law and exemption under PF law are two different statutory requirements. Compliance with one framework does not automatically satisfy the requirements of the other.Consequently, certain establishments continued operating as recognised PF trusts without obtaining the requisite exemption notification from the appropriate Government as stipulated in the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (the ‘EPF Act’) or corresponding exemption framework under the Code on Social Security, 2020. This created a legacy compliance gap and potential regulatory exposure, notwithstanding that the PF contributions may have been deposited into the trust and employees were receiving PF benefits.Recognising the need to address these historical arrangements, the Government introduced the EPFO Amnesty Scheme, 2026 under the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 2026. The opportunity is significant, but time bound. The Scheme was notified on 29 June 2026 for a six-month window which is getting over on 28 December 2026, unless extended in accordance with its terms.The significance of Amnesty Scheme, 2026 therefore extends beyond regularising a missing approval. For eligible employers, it offers an opportunity to address historical regulatory uncertainty, validate member-level PF compliance and decide whether an employer-managed trust remains the right model for the future.Who does Amnesty Scheme, 2026 cover?Amnesty Scheme, 2026 applies to establishments that have been operating a PF trust on the basis of recognition under the Income-tax Act, 1961 but do not have a formal notification granting exemption from the appropriate Government under the Code on Social Security, 2020 or erstwhile EPF Act.The Scheme gives eligible establishments a one-time opportunity to regularise their historical exemption status and bring their PF arrangements within the statutory framework.Section 143 of the Code retains a key safeguard for the employees: exemption is conditional on employees receiving benefits that are substantially similar or superior to those available under the statutory framework. Regularisation is therefore not simply a documentation exercise, the underlying contributions, interest, member balances and trust administration remain central.Which employers should assess eligibility?Employers should begin their eligibility assessment with three key questions:Does the establishment currently operate, or has it previously operated a PF trust?Was the trust recognised under the legacy Income-tax framework? Has the appropriate Government issued a formal PF exemption notification?Where Income-tax recognition is in place, but the exemption notification cannot be located, the establishment should not assume that tax recognition satisfied the exemption requirement under PF statute. A thorough review should encompass trust deeds, exemption applications, tax-recognition orders, EPFO correspondence, regional EPFO records and both pending and completed assessment proceedings.This review may be more complex where the business has undergone mergers, demergers, transfers, closures, payroll migrations or changes in employee population. In such cases, the history of exemptions and member accounts must be traced across the relevant legal entities and periods involved.Two options after regularising the trust’s past exemption statusAmnesty Scheme, 2026 divides eligible establishments into two categories based on how they plan to meet their PF obligations after regularising their past exemption status.Category I: regularise past exemption status and move to direct EPFO complianceCategory I covers establishments that want to regularise their past exemption status and have already begun, or plan to begin, complying directly with the EPFO framework as un-exempted establishments. In simple terms, the employer regularises the period when the PF trust operated and meets future PF obligations directly through EPFO.These employers must transfer the trust’s accumulated funds and reconcile the records for each employee. Obtaining an order alone does not complete the process. Member balances, interest, settlements and any applicable pension allocations must be correctly matched to each member and transferred under the prescribed process.Category II: regularise past exemption status and continue the exempt PF trustCategory II covers establishments that want to regularise their past exemption status and continue operating an exempt PF trust. This option may suit organisations with well-established trustee oversight, strong investment systems and the capacity to manage member accounts and claims.The employer should not assume that continuing with the trust is the right choice. It must assess whether the trust can keep meeting the applicable requirements for benefits, governance, audits, investments, reporting and member services. A trust that is difficult to manage today may remain a compliance risk even after its past exemption status is regularised.The choice between continuing an exempt trust and moving to un-exempted compliance should therefore consider governance capability, administrative cost, investment oversight, employee servicing and the organisation’s longer-term compliance model.What eligible employers stand to gainIn addition to regularising past exemption status, Amnesty Scheme, 2026 provides certain benefits listed below. Each benefit is subject to the Scheme’s eligibility criteria, conditions, audit requirements and employer responsibilities.Potential benefitWhat it meansRegularising past exemption statusExemption status and trust recognition may be granted for the period from the date the trust began operating to the applicable cut-off date.Relaxed eligibility requirementsEligible establishments do not have to meet the usual minimum requirements for the number of employees and the size of the trust’s accumulated funds.Three-year requirement treated as metFor eligible Category-I establishments, the Scheme provides relaxation by allowing the period for which the PF trust has already been operating to be counted towards the three-year requirement. Consequently, an eligible employer need not necessarily wait for another three years to complete this condition before seeking exemption.In other words, the Scheme helps eligible employers overcome the waiting-period requirement, rather than making them start their three-year compliance history afresh.Relief from pending proceedingsQualifying pending assessments for PF dues, interest and damages arising from the lack of a formal exemption may be withdrawn and brought to an end. This relief is available only if member accounts receive contributions and interest at statutory or higher levels and the Scheme’s other conditions are met.Relief in completed assessmentsA qualifying completed assessment order may be treated as void from inception. Any amount already recovered under such an order may be adjusted against the establishment’s future dues, subject to the applicable appeal provisions.Options for future PF complianceAfter regularising past exemption status, the employer may meet future PF obligations directly through EPFO as an un-exempted establishment (Category I) or continue operating an exempt PF trust (Category II). Both options are subject to the applicable conditions.Regularising specified pension casesTransfers to the applicable Employees’ Pension Scheme may be allowed for non-excluded employees who were in eligible service on the cut-off date and should have been enrolled earlier.Important limits: the Amnesty Scheme, 2026 does not resolve all PF compliance issuesImportantly, Amnesty Scheme, 2026 is not a general waiver of historical PF defaults. Its principal purpose is to regularise the exemption status of eligible legacy PF trusts. Employees who were left out of PF coverage and delays in transferring amounts from the establishment to the trust may still require assessment and corrective action.The employer must also cover any shortfall in past contributions or interest credited below the required level. Any deviation from the prescribed investment pattern may attract the applicable surcharge or penalty, and the employer may also be required to make good losses arising from the trust’s investment transactions. The employer may remain responsible for unresolved member accounts, audit findings and disputes about membership, service or benefits.The key question is not just, “Can the organisation file an application?” It is, “Can the organisation show that employees received the contributions, interest and benefits due to them, with records for each member to support this?”A separate window for damages disputesAmnesty Scheme, 2026 forms part of a broader EPFO effort to address legacy compliance. VISHWAS 2026, which is also scheduled to remain open until 28 December 2026, provides a separate settlement mechanism for eligible historical disputes involving damages or penalties. The schemes serve different purposes: Amnesty addresses the exemption status of qualifying PF trusts, whereas VISHWAS addresses eligible damages and penalty disputes. An establishment facing both the issues may therefore need to evaluate the schemes separately.Underlying records may be as important as the applicationAn establishment applying under the Amensty Scheme, 2026 must gather details of employees contributing to the fund, employees in service on the relevant cut-off date and former employees whose accounts have not been settled. The trust’s financial statements and each member’s account records must be ready for audit and reconciliation.An audit by a Chartered Accountant is mandatory. If EPFO requires a Compliance Audit or Special Audit, it must be completed within three months of the application. The establishment must pay for the Special Audit.The employer should also have the following records ready: Income-tax recognition records, trust deeds, investment statements, contribution and interest calculations, withdrawal and settlement details, pension-allocation data and KYC records. It should also explain any gaps in past records. These records are especially important where the trust has used different payroll systems, or the business has undergone corporate restructuring.From trust to EPFO: how are the accumulated funds transferred?For Category I establishments, regularising past exemption status is only part of the process. The accumulated balances must also be transferred to the statutory fund using the prescribed process and within the notified timeline. EPFO can help credit these balances to individual accounts, but the employer must first confirm the correct amount for each member.Knowing the trust’s total accumulated funds is not enough. For each member, the opening and closing balances must be reconciled with employee and employer contributions, interest, withdrawals, settlements and pension allocations. The employer may remain responsible for any shortfall or other issues identified during this process.How the Scheme affects employeesFor employees, regularisation mainly helps protect the retirement savings they have built up and brings the trust’s legal status into line with how member accounts are managed.The Scheme does not automatically entitle employees to an extra payment or guarantee that every past claim will be settled immediately. The outcome depends on the available records, the type of shortfall or other issues and whether the regularisation conditions are met. If contributions or interest are below the required level, the employer remains responsible for covering the shortfall.Clear communication with employees is also important. A move to direct EPFO compliance as an un-exempted establishment may require explanations of balance transfers, UAN mapping, pension allocation and future claims. If the exempt trust continues, employees should understand how their accounts, interest and claims will be managed after regularisation.Why the decision involves more than legal complianceImplementing the Amensty Scheme, 2026 requires HR, payroll, finance, tax, legal and treasury teams, trustees and external auditors to work together. HR and payroll teams must check employees’ membership and contribution histories. Finance and treasury teams need to reconcile investments and accumulated fund balances. Trustees must provide supporting records for each member and for unsettled claims. Legal and tax teams must establish the history of the trust’s recognition and exemption status.Category II employers should also assess whether continuing an exempt trust is practical. An exempt trust may give employers closer control over administration and allow them to tailor services to members’ needs. However, it also brings ongoing duties to act in members’ interests and meet investment, accounting, audit and reporting requirements. In some cases, direct EPFO compliance may be a more sustainable long-term option.A practical roadmap before 28 December 2026Employers should begin preparing well before 28 December 2026, rather than wait until the deadline. Start by checking the trust’s legal status and choosing Category I or Category II. Then reconstruct member records, check contributions and interest, review investments, complete the required audit, correct any shortfalls or other issues and submit the formal application with supporting records.The formal application must follow the prescribed process and should be submitted through the relevant EPFO Regional Office. An expression of interest may help start discussions with EPFO, but it does not replace the formal application.The Scheme provides for a final order on whether the application is admissible within six months of receiving a complete application. Employers should therefore include all supporting records when they first apply. Incomplete member records or unexplained differences in financial figures can delay the review and weaken the establishment’s position.An opportunity to resolve past issues and improve future complianceAmnesty Scheme, 2026 value goes beyond obtaining an exemption order. Employers must use this opportunity to check what each member is entitled to, reconcile past records, correct shortfalls and choose a sustainable approach to future PF compliance. This means either continuing the exempt PF trust or moving to direct EPFO compliance as an un-exempted establishment.Delaying action can make it harder for qualifying organisations to reconstruct past records, leaves member balances unresolved and prolongs regulatory risks. With the Scheme scheduled to close on 28 December 2026, employers should begin assessing eligibility, planning audits and reconciling records immediately.The strongest outcome will not be an order that merely regularises the past. It will be a PF arrangement that can demonstrate, member by member, that contributions and interest were protected, deficiencies were corrected and future governance is sustainable. Amnesty Scheme, 2026 should therefore be approached not as a filing concession, but as a final opportunity to convert a legacy exemption gap into a credible, employee-focused compliance framework.(The author, Ravi Jain is Tax Partner at Vialto. Vikas Kumar, Director, and Pawan Digga, Manager at Vialto, have also contributed to this article. Views are personal.)Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Trump takes Thanksgiving swipe at New York Times reporter: ‘Lowlife’
articles.summary: President Trump attacked New York Times reporter David Sanger as a “lowlife” early Thursday, after the outlet published an analysis about the president’s varying success on moving markets and other economic issues. The president called Sanger “mediocre” in a Truth Social post Thursday, saying the Times journalist was not covering his administration’s wins on issues like…
articles.body:
President Trump attacked New York Times reporter David Sanger as a “lowlife” early Thursday, after the outlet published an analysis about the president’s varying success on moving markets and other economic issues.

The president called Sanger “mediocre” in a Truth Social post Thursday, saying the Times journalist was not covering his administration’s wins on issues like immigration, the Venezuelan strike and the planned detonation of lead azide in Iowa.

“David Sanger is a lowlife that only writes what he is told to write by his bosses,” the president wrote. “Also, until the Election, best Market, EVER, 82 days, settled 8 Wars, and the USA is respected again like never before!”

Sanger’s piece, published Wednesday, examined how the president has sought to both take credit for upticks in the stock market through his economic or foreign policy intervention while also distancing himself from backslides when the stock market is doing poorly.

The reporter used the example of Nvidia’s initial surge then decline as one example, with Trump touting the stock’s rebound after his administration worked to reinstall Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang before blaming the midterm results for the stock market’s dip later in the week.

The outlet pushed back on Trump’s criticism in a statement to The Hill on Thursday.

“If readers want to understand the market effects of President Trump’s interventions, including Nvidia’s reversal, his disruption of international trade, and his decision to go to war with Iran, then David Sanger’s latest report is an essential read,” the statement reads.

“David has covered five American presidents in more than four decades at The Times; his coverage of the ways in which the administration is shaping foreign policy and national security is unmatched,” it continues. “Noisy name-calling is just an attempt to distract from the news.”

A source familiar with the matter told The Hill on Monday that Vice President Vance was personally involved in helping Huang get his job back at Nvidia after the chief executive stepped down earlier this month following revelations of affairs with several women, including one who had ties to Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia’s stock closed at about $126 a share at the end of regular trading hours Friday, rebounding to more than $166 around the beginning of regular trading hours Monday. However, the AI firm’s stock slowly dropped again, ending at $149 a share at the end of trading hours Wednesday.

It’s not the first time the president has taken swipes at Sanger, his colleagues or other media outlets broadly. He described Sanger as “treasonous” in May after the Times reporter noted that the U.S. had not achieved the political change the administration was looking for amid the Iran war.

“I had a total military victory, but the fake news, guys like you, write incorrectly,” Trump told him on Air Force One during a trip back from China.

articles.title: Trump Says Revised GDP Numbers ‘Fake,’ Calls for Investigation
articles.summary: President Donald Trump accused his own administration of a “purposeful” move to under-report US economic growth, seizing on a routine data revision to underp...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump accused his own administration of a "purposeful" move to under-report US economic growth, seizing on a routine data revision to underpin an allegation of election interference with no evidence.

In a social media post on Thursday, Trump pointed to GDP figures that showed the economy grew 4.3% annualized in the third quarter — revised from the 3.4% estimate in a previous release — saying it's a "major difference."

"It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE," he said without offering proof.

"I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation. This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error," the president added in the post, which was sent from his West Palm Beach golf course on the morning of the US Thanksgiving holiday.

Trump has long stoked fringe or conspiratorial explanations for election defeats, though has previously chalked up this month's midterm rout to the fact he was not personally on the ballot.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes GDP figures in stages, and the headline number often moves as the agency factors in additional data.

Trump has complained about unflattering economic numbers in the past. Last year, he fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a report showed weak job growth.

articles.body:
President Trump on Thursday called for an investigation into economic data released ahead of the midterm elections after the federal government revised its estimate of third-quarter growth upward.

The president, in a Thanksgiving Day post on Truth Social , alleged without providing evidence that the initial gross domestic product (GDP) figures were deliberately understated.

“Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error.”

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) said Wednesday that the economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.3 percent between July and September, up from its initial estimate of 3.4 percent.

GDP estimates are routinely revised as more comprehensive data becomes available. The BEA is scheduled to release another estimate next month.

“The American Economy under The Trump Administration is doing FAR BETTER than the good numbers already released,” Trump continued in his post.

The demand for a probe follows a tough midterm election cycle for Republicans, who lost control of both the House and Senate as Democrats made affordability a central focus of their campaigns.

The economy was a top concern for voters, many of whom expressed frustration with rising prices. Trump’s sweeping tariffs and the economic fallout from the war with Iran also weighed on Americans.

While the economy has continued to grow, fueled in part by investments in artificial intelligence, inflation remains stubbornly high.

Separate data released Wednesday showed the personal consumption expenditures price index — the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge — rose 3.8 percent annually in October, in line with expectations but well above the central bank’s 2 percent target.

The data has also fueled expectations that the Fed could raise interest rates at its meeting next month after holding them steady in October.

articles.title: Kroger supermarket employees get unhappy Thanksgiving message: You’re fired
articles.summary: The cuts are the first of 3,000 layoffs to take place through 2029
articles.body:
Kroger's cuts have begun a month after CEO Greg Foran announced 3,000 corporate employees would lose their jobs over the next three years.

The Cincinnati-based company laid off an "unspecified" number of employees in its first wave of cuts, just before the Thanksgiving holiday, a company representative confirmed with Restaurant Dive this week .

"This lets us move vital resources closer to the customer to lower prices, invest in our associates and create a better shopping experience," Foran said last month in a company memo.

The cuts are part of Kroger's wider efficiency focus, which Foran pitched during the company's Investor Day call in late October - move quickly and cut resources that slow things down.

"When something works, scale it fast," Foran said. "When it does not, end it fast. These are not easy decisions. But if we're asking the organization to move faster, we cannot keep work, assets, and layers that distract us from building America's favorite grocer."

Layoffs have swept across the grocery industry over the past year amid tighter consumer spending and competition.

Regional grocer Winn-Dixie closed its Alabama stores at the end of 2025 and slashed corporate jobs at its Jacksonville headquarters in February .

Bargain supermarket Grocery Outlet revealed in March plans to shutter 36 underperforming stores after CEO Jason Potter said the company expanded too fast in the eastern United States.

And grocer Albertsons has laid off 873 employees through October 2026.

Consumers have taken a frugal approach to buying groceries in a year in which gas prices have averaged more than $4 a gallon for more days in 2026 than any other year in history, according to fuel-price tracking site GasBuddy.

Inflation hit three-year highs in May and September , and the latest inflation report from the Department of Commerce indicates it didn't let up in October .

Record-breaking diesel prices have increased the cost of food production and transportation, which cuts into grocery stores' profits, Yahoo Finance reported in October.

Kroger's CEO believes the company can overcome these headwinds with efficiency, but the grocer's earnings are still suffering. Since Foran took the helm in February, Kroger's sales increased 1 percent from February to April and 0.2 percent from May to July, according to company earnings reports .

articles.title: Thanksgiving Storm Sweeps East Coast, Delays Macy’s 100th Parade
articles.summary: A powerful Thanksgiving storm is sweeping up the US East Coast toward New York, as adverse weather knocks out power to more than half a million homes and bus...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- A powerful Thanksgiving storm is sweeping up the US East Coast toward New York, as adverse weather knocks out power to more than half a million homes and businesses across the nation while snarling holiday travel.

The strengthening storm has already led to the postponement of events including Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade, which has rescheduled for Saturday, marking the first time the annual holiday procession has been delayed. The governors of New York and New Jersey both declared a state of emergency ahead of the storm, warning of damaging winds, heavy rainfall and severe coastal flooding through Friday.

The conditions complicate journeys for those heading to family gatherings, though the days leading up to Thanksgiving tend to see greater travel than the holiday itself. AccuWeather meteorologist Alyssa Glenny said wind gusts have already reached 72 miles per hour at Stingray Point, Virginia, with coastal areas of New Jersey and Long Island bracing for gusts up to 80 mph as the storm pushes northward.

"We're looking at the afternoon going into the evening for peak rainfall in New York," Glenny said via telephone. "Once we get to midday, early afternoon, the wind is going to pick up and then the next 12 hours is the window for peak winds."

There were about 400 reported flight cancellations across the US, with Baltimore/Washington International Airport and New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport among the worst impacted, according to FlightAware data. While elevated, the disruption is far below the levels recorded earlier this month after the US Federal Aviation Administration imposed a nationwide ground stop due to an equipment outage.

Meanwhile, there are over 560,000 US power outages as of 10:50 a.m. Eastern Time, according to PowerOutage.com. That includes about 5% of customers in Virginia and Missouri, with the latter enduring heavy snowfall from a winter storm.

"With the power outages, we always are concerned with downed trees that could impact travel," AccuWeather's Glenny said. "Along the coastal areas — like those locations in Southern New Jersey, Ocean City, Maryland where they're having the coastal flooding — there are definitely some travel impacts with flooded roadways in that corridor."

articles.title: Domestic LPG production up 25% y-o-y during April-October
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s domestic production of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has increased by nearly 25% year-on-year to a record 9.2 million tonne in the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s domestic production of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has increased by nearly 25% year-on-year to a record 9.2 million tonne in the first seven months of this financial year, while consumption has fallen by 15% and imports have remained subdued due to supply disruptions from West Asia amid the ongoing conflict.Indian refineries are now producing nearly 43,000 tonne of LPG per day, up from about 34,000 tonne last year, to meet demand for cooking and heating fuel, as imports have fallen by more than 40%, from 13 MT to 7.6 MT. Before the US-Iran conflict broke out, India imported nearly 60% of its LPG consumption, with 90% of these supplies coming from West Asian countries such as the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia through the Strait of Hormuz.Compared with 13 MT during Apr-Oct in FY26, LPG imports during the corresponding period this year fell to 7.6 MT. In Oct this year, 1.3 MT of LPG was imported against 1.9 MT a year ago.Refiners ramped up LPG production to 55,000 tonne per day after the closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted supplies by more than 60% in March and April due to the conflict. Following directions from govt, molecules used for petrochemical production were diverted to LPG manufacturing to ensure there was no shortage of cooking gas. As supplies of imported LPG improved, refiners scaled down production but are still maintaining daily output at an average 25% higher than pre-war levels.Govt also put in place a new mechanism in Aug this year to ramp up domestic LPG production during periods of tight supply, setting facility-wise output levels for refineries and upstream companies whenever required.LPG is the primary cooking fuel for more than 32.6 crore households in the country, including about 10.6 crore beneficiaries of the PM Ujjwala Yojana, who receive a subsidy on their gas cylinders.Govt’s push towards natural gas to reduce dependence on LPG imports is also reflected in consumption, which has fallen by over 15% to 16.2 MT between Apr and Oct, from 19.1 MT a year ago.
